points.why: It describes the reinforcing loop of fewer findings, more trust, less scrutiny and a cleaner record, and notes a clean record looks the same whether the code is good or nobody is looking.

It proposes auditing each check's boundary and kind, calls more unit tests the same kind of check run harder, and recommends canary rollout with auto-rollback, schema checks and real-environment validation.
It ties review depth to stakes rather than track record, with fixed-rate sampled reviews, a minimum review time, an explicit confirmation flag and a second approver for checkout config.
It tracks review time, comments per PR and silent-approval rate with drift alerts, explicitly rejects blaming the reviewer, and calls the agent right most of the time.

pitfalls.why: It calls the four-minute approval the loop working as designed and warns against 'reviewer should have looked harder.'
It opens by saying more unit tests are not enough and lists structural actions beyond them.

notes: It assumes the agent wrote the tests as well as the change and says review has 'stopped doing anything', both stated with more certainty than the user's summary supports, though it does flag that it lacks the timeline.
